After loading the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill, refresh the registry (`uip maestro flow registry pull --force`) so the just-deployed agent is discoverable, then author the flow per the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill's workflow. Done when the requested `.flow` file exists and `uip maestro flow validate` passes on it.
227	
228	Read the relevant reference file at each step — do not guess.
229	
230	## Quick Start: Scenario 2 — In-Solution Coded Agent in a Flow
231	
232	Use when the coded agent is tightly coupled to one flow and lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution. The agent is wired to the flow via `--local` registry discovery — no separate Orchestrator deployment for the agent, no separate skill hand-off. **`uipath-agents` owns this scenario end-to-end** — solution scaffolding, flow scaffolding, agent build, registration, and flow wiring all happen here. Do not invoke `uipath-maestro-flow` as a separate skill; run the maestro-flow CLI commands directly from this workflow.
233	
234	Execute the following in order, end-to-end, in one pass — do not pause for confirmation between steps.
235	
236	1. **Scaffold the solution.** From the working directory:
237	
238	   ```bash
239	   uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
240	   ```
241	
242	   Creates `<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. All subsequent project paths are relative to the solution root.
243	
244	2. **Scaffold the flow project inside the solution** (the layout is always double-nested `<Solution>/<Flow>/<Flow>.flow`):
245	
246	   ```bash
247	   cd "<SolutionName>"
248	   uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>" --output json
249	   ```
250	
251	   This auto-registers the flow as a project in the solution.
252	
253	3. **Scaffold the coded agent as a sibling folder.** From the solution root (still inside `<SolutionName>/`):
254	
255	   ```bash
256	   uv venv --python 3.13
257	   source .venv/bin/activate        # .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
258	   uv add <framework-package>       # e.g. uipath-langchain for LangGraph
259	   uv add uipath-dev --dev
260	   uv sync
261	   uip codedagent setup --force
262	   uip codedagent new "<AgentName>"
263	   ```
264	
265	   Result: `<SolutionName>/<AgentName>/` sibling to `<SolutionName>/<FlowName>/`.
266	
267	4. **Implement the agent's `main.py`** with lazy LLM initialization (LLM clients inside graph nodes only — never at module top level), then regenerate entry-points / bindings:
268	
269	   ```bash
270	   cd "<AgentName>"
271	   uip codedagent init
272	   ```
273	
274	   Refer to [frameworks/](frameworks/) for the chosen framework's patterns. Verify locally with `uip codedagent run <entrypoint> '<input>'`.
275	
276	5. **Register the agent in the solution.** This step mints the `resource.key` UUID the flow node will reference:
277	
278	   ```bash
279	   cd ..
280	   uip solution project add "<AgentName>" "<SolutionName>.uipx" --output json
281	   ```
282	
283	   After this command, `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<AgentName>.json` holds the `resource.key`. Read that file (or the `--output json` response) to capture the UUID — it is what the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey` will reference.
284	
285	6. **Discover the agent's flow-side definition** (no `uip login` required for `--local`):
286	
287	   ```bash
288	   cd "<FlowName>"
289	   uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
290	   uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json
291	   ```
292	
293	   The second command's `Data.Node` object is what gets pasted verbatim into the flow's top-level `definitions[]` array.
294	
295	7. **Wire the agent node into the `.flow` file.** Edit `<FlowName>.flow` directly:
296	   - Add a `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` node to `nodes[]` with one `inputs.<field>` entry per property in the agent's input schema (see step 6's `Data.Node.inputDefinition`) and `model.section: "In this solution"`.
297	   - For input field values, see [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs).
298	   - Add the definition from step 6 to `definitions[]`.
299	   - Add a top-level `bindings[]` entry for the agent (no duplicates per `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)`).
300	   - Add edges from upstream nodes to the agent's input port and from its output port downstream.
301	   - To surface the agent's output as a flow-level result, declare an `out` global and map it on the End node with `"source": "=js:$vars.<agentNodeId>.output.<field>"` (outputs DO use `=js:`; only inputs do not).
302	
303	   See [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md) for the directory layout and [flow-integration.md § Pattern 1](flow-integration.md#pattern-1-in-solution-coded-agent) for the JSON shape.
304	
305	8. **Validate and format:**
306	
307	   ```bash
308	   uip maestro flow validate "<FlowName>.flow" --output json
309	   uip maestro flow format "<FlowName>.flow" --output json
310	   ```
311	
312	   Resolve any validation errors before declaring the scenario complete. Done when both commands return success and the flow file contains the wired agent node.
313	
314	## Framework Selection
315	
316	> **First — is this an agent at all?** If the task is deterministic logic with no LLM reasoning (validate data, call an API with custom auth, transform records, upload/download files), it's a **Python Coded Function** — not an agent. Use the [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions) skill instead of this one. Coded Functions use typed I/O (`@dataclass`, Pydantic `BaseModel`, or a thin Python class with typed annotations) and a `functions` map in `uipath.json`; what distinguishes an agent is LLM reasoning and a framework graph.
317	
318	If the task needs LLM reasoning, infer the framework from the user's prompt when possible. If ambiguous, ask them to choose:
319	
320	1. **LangGraph** (recommended — best integrated with the UiPath ecosystem) — StateGraph with conditional routing, tool use, interrupts. Best for complex LLM agents.
321	2. **LlamaIndex** — Workflow with events and RAG support. Most complete LangGraph alternative.
322	3. **OpenAI Agents** — Lightweight agent with tools and handoffs. Best for simple LLM agents; lacks HITL, process invocation, and state persistence.
323	
324	**Inference hints:** mentions of tools/tool calling, multi-step, or orchestration → LangGraph. Simple handoffs or lightweight LLM → OpenAI Agents. No LLM needed → not an agent — use [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions). Summarize / research / synthesize over PDF or TXT (incl. bucket files, attachments) → not a framework choice — see [capabilities/deeprag/planning.md](capabilities/deeprag/planning.md). Per-row CSV extraction → see [capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md](capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md). When in doubt, ask.
325	
326	**Always tell the user which framework you selected and why** before proceeding to build. Example: "I'll use **LangGraph** for this agent since it involves tool calling and multi-step orchestration."
327	
328	## Troubleshooting
329	
330	| Error | Cause | Solution |
331	|-------|-------|----------|
332	| `Project authors cannot be empty` | Missing `authors` in `pyproject.toml` | Add `authors = [{ name = "Your Name" }]` to `[project]` section |
333	| `Version already exists` on deploy | Same version already published | Bump patch version in `pyproject.toml` before re-deploying |
334	| `Your local version is behind...Aborted!` | Push needs interactive confirmation | Use `uip codedagent push --overwrite` to force push |
335

338	- **UiPath Python SDK**: https://uipath.github.io/uipath-python/
339	- **UiPath Evaluations**: https://uipath.github.io/uipath-python/eval/

1	# Setup UiPath Agent Project
2	
3	## Preflight
4	
5	```bash
6	python --version                                           # 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13
7	which uv  > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "install uv:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh"
8	which uip > /dev/null 2>&1 || echo "install uip: npm install -g @uipath/cli"
9	```
10	
11	## Framework Selection
12	
13	Pick the framework before starting. The package installed in the Workflow determines which scaffold `uip codedagent new` produces.
14	
15	| Agent Type | `<FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>` | Framework config | Guide |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| LangGraph | `"uipath-langchain"` | `langgraph.json` | [langgraph-integration.md](../frameworks/langgraph-integration.md) |
18	| LlamaIndex | `uipath-llamaindex` | `llama_index.json` | [llamaindex-integration.md](../frameworks/llamaindex-integration.md) |
19	| OpenAI Agents | `uipath-openai-agents` | `openai_agents.json` | [openai-agents-integration.md](../frameworks/openai-agents-integration.md) |
20	
21	## Starting Points
22	
23	| Starting from | Use |
24	|---|---|
25	| Empty directory | The Workflow below |
26	| Existing UiPath agent (has `main.py` + `<framework>.json` + UiPath deps) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` only |
27	| Existing Python agent (has `main.py`, missing UiPath deps / framework config) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, `uv add <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>`, adapt `main.py` per the framework guide, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` |
28	| Studio Web Local Workspace solution (ancestor contains `.sw-path-marker` or `.local/folder.lock`) | Already scaffolded by Studio Web. One-time local-run prep: `uv venv --python 3.13`, activate, `uv sync`, `uip codedagent setup --force`. Do **not** run `uip codedagent new`. Re-run `init` after every edit that adds/removes/renames/retypes a field on `Input`/`Output`/`State` or changes the entry-function signature — see [local-workspace.md](local-workspace.md) § Schema Sync After Edits for the full rule and anti-patterns. |
29	
30	## Workflow
31	
32	```bash
33	mkdir <PROJECT_NAME> && cd <PROJECT_NAME>
34	uv venv --python 3.13                        # uv defaults to the latest Python; pin to a UiPath-supported version
35	source .venv/bin/activate                    # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
36	uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>
37	uip codedagent setup --force
38	uip codedagent new <PROJECT_NAME>
39	uv add uipath-dev --dev                      # required by `uip codedagent dev` (local dev web server)
40	uv sync
41	uip codedagent init
42	```
43	
44	`uipath-dev` is added to the dev dependency group during scaffold so `uip codedagent dev` works later without a second install pass. Skipping it causes `uip codedagent dev` to fail with *"The 'uipath-dev' package is required to use the dev command"*.
45	
46	**What `uip codedagent setup` does:** locates a Python that has `uipath` installed and caches its path, so later commands (`init`/`run`/`eval`/`pack`) can invoke the Python SDK. It searches PATH (`python3.x`, `python3`, `python`) and uses your `.venv` only when activated. So when using uv, always `uv sync` then activate the venv before the `setup` command.
47	
48	## Coded Function Agents
49	
50	`uipath.json` carries the entrypoint mapping:
51	
52	```json
53	{
54	  "functions": {
55	    "main": "main.py:main"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Edit the scaffolded `main.py`'s `Input` / `Output` models and `async def main` to fit the real agent.
61	
62	## Generated Files
63	
64	| File | Purpose |
65	|---|---|
66	| `pyproject.toml` | Project metadata and dependencies |
67	| `main.py` | Agent entrypoint |
68	| `<framework>.json` | Framework config (LangGraph / LlamaIndex / OpenAI Agents) |
69	| `uipath.json` | Runtime options, pack options, `functions` map |
70	| `entry-points.json` | Input / output schemas from Pydantic models |
71	| `bindings.json` | Runtime bindings |
72	| `uv.lock` | Dependency lockfile |
73	| `.uipath/telemetry.json` | Telemetry configuration |
74	| `AGENTS.md`, `.agent/` | Documentation |
75	
76	## `uipath.json`
77	
78	```json
79	{
80	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
81	  "runtimeOptions": {
82	    "isConversational": false
83	  },
84	  "packOptions": {
85	    "fileExtensionsIncluded": [],
86	    "filesIncluded": [],
87	    "filesExcluded": [],
88	    "directoriesExcluded": [],
89	    "includeUvLock": true
90	  },
91	  "functions": {}
92	}
93	```
94	
95	**Key fields:**
96	- **`runtimeOptions.isConversational`** - scaffold defaults to `false` (single-shot). Building a chat/conversational agent? Flip to `true` BEFORE `uip codedagent init` so `entry-points.json` gets the chat shape. See [conversational-agents](../capabilities/conversational-agents.md).
97	- **`packOptions`** - Control which files are included when packaging for deployment
98	- **`functions`** - Entrypoint mappings (format: `"file_path:function_name"`)
99	
100	### `packOptions.directoriesExcluded` for solution context
101	
102	When the agent project is registered in a solution and uploaded via `uip solution upload`, the agent directory is bundled into the solution archive. Set `directoriesExcluded` to keep Python build artifacts out of the archive:
103	
104	```json
105	"packOptions": {
106	  "directoriesExcluded": [".venv", "__pycache__"],
107	  "includeUvLock": true
108	}
109	```
110	
111	`.venv/` is hundreds of MB of installed wheels and breaks uploads. `__pycache__/` is ephemeral bytecode. Both regenerate from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` on the target side. Without these exclusions, `uip solution upload` produces an oversized archive that can be rejected by Studio Web.
112	
113	- `isConversational: true` for chat-style agents.
114	- `packOptions` controls `.nupkg` contents at deploy time.
115	
116	## Troubleshooting
117	
118	| Error | Cause | Fix |
119	|---|---|---|
120	| `uipath executable not found` | `setup` not run, or run without venv activated | Activate `.venv` and re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
121	| UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or `uipathExePath` is stale | The CLI still points at an old or missing virtualenv executable | Run `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force` to refresh `uipathExePath` |
122	| `Found .venv in current directory but no virtual environment is activated` | `.venv` exists but `VIRTUAL_ENV` is unset | Activate `.venv` first, then re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
123	| `No compatible Python installation found` | Python outside 3.11 – 3.13 | Install 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13 (or set `PYTHON_TOOL_PYTHON_VERSIONS`) |
124	| `Project authors cannot be empty` | Missing `authors` in `pyproject.toml` | Add `authors = [{ name = "Your Name" }]` to `[project]` |
125	| `NameError` during `init` | Framework not installed when `init` imports `main.py` | Run `uv sync` before `uip codedagent init` |
126	| `No entrypoints found in uipath.json` | Framework config or package missing | Verify `uv pip install` succeeded, then re-run `uip codedagent init` |
127	| `ModuleNotFoundError` for a package you just installed, even after activating `.venv` | A shell `python` alias points at a different interpreter (uv-managed, system, etc.) | Use `.venv/bin/python` directly for sanity checks, or `unalias python` for the session |

1	# Coded Agents in Flow Projects (Sibling Folder)
2	
3	A coded agent can live as a sibling folder to a flow project inside the same solution. The flow references it via `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` with `section: "In this solution"`. The flow's `uip maestro flow registry list --local` discovers the agent by reading `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`, written by `uip solution project add`.
4	
5	For the published-agent path (deployed standalone via `uip codedagent deploy`), see [coded/flow-integration.md § Pattern 2](flow-integration.md#pattern-2-published-coded-agent).
6	
7	## Sibling Folder Structure
8	
9	The `<resourceKey>` is the local UUID minted by `uip solution project add` — stable the moment the agent joins the solution.
10	
11	```
12	<SolutionDir>/
13	├── <SolutionName>.uipx
14	├── resources/                      # created and maintained by `uip solution project add`
15	│   └── solution_folder/
16	│       ├── process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json   # holds the `resource.key` UUID
17	│       └── package/<CodedAgentProject>.json
18	├── <FlowProject>/
19	│   ├── <FlowName>.flow
20	│   └── project.uiproj
21	└── <CodedAgentProject>/
22	    ├── main.py                     # agent entrypoint
23	    ├── pyproject.toml              # Python project config
24	    ├── uipath.json                 # UiPath project config
25	    ├── entry-points.json           # generated by `uip codedagent init`
26	    ├── bindings.json               # runtime bindings
27	    ├── main.mermaid                # generated graph diagram
28	    ├── project.uiproj              # Studio Web project metadata
29	    ├── .env                        # environment variables
30	    ├── .uipath/
31	    │   └── telemetry.json          # telemetry config
32	    └── .venv/                      # local virtualenv (created by `uv sync`)
33	```
34	
35	### Key differences from a published coded agent
36	
37	- **`resource.key`** is minted locally at `uip solution project add` time, not by Orchestrator at `uip codedagent deploy` time
38	- **No `codedagent deploy`** — the agent ships inside the solution package
39	- **Registry discovery is `--local`** (reads `resources/solution_folder/process/` files); no login or `registry pull` required
40	- **`model.section`** is `"In this solution"`
41	
42	## Scaffolding the Sibling-Folder Coded Agent
43	
44	The full end-to-end workflow (solution init → flow scaffold → agent scaffold → register → wire → validate) is owned by [`quickstart.md` § Scenario 2](quickstart.md#quick-start-scenario-2--in-solution-coded-agent-in-a-flow). This file covers the agent-side detail of step 3 (scaffold) and step 5 (registration) in finer detail; the canonical sequence stays in the quickstart so it remains executable in one pass.
45	
46	If the solution and flow project don't yet exist, run `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` and then `uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>"` from inside the solution **before** the steps below — those calls are the start of Scenario 2.
47	
48	1. From the solution directory, create the agent folder and scaffold inside it:
49	
50	   ```bash
51	   mkdir <CodedAgentProject>
52	   cd <CodedAgentProject>
53	   uv venv --python 3.13
54	   source .venv/bin/activate       # .venv/Scripts/activate on Windows
55	   uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>   # e.g. uipath for Coded Function
56	   uip codedagent setup --force
57	   uip codedagent new <agent-name>
58	   uv sync
59	   ```
60	
61	   For a simple stub with no LLM call, use the Coded Function framework
62	   (`uipath` package). This avoids downloading the full LangGraph or
63	   LlamaIndex stack and keeps the setup fast.
64	
65	2. Implement `main.py`. Use lazy LLM initialization (create clients inside functions, never at module level).
66	
67	3. Generate entry points:
68	
69	   ```bash
70	   uip codedagent init
71	   ```
72	
73	4. Register the agent in the solution — **this is the step that mints the `resource.key`** the flow will reference:
74	
75	   ```bash
76	   cd <SolutionDir>
77	   uip solution project add <CodedAgentProject> <SolutionName>.uipx --output json
78	   ```
79	
80	   After this command, `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json` holds the `resource.key` UUID.
81	
82	
83	### Flow Discovery
84	
85	From inside the flow project directory, the agent is discoverable via the in-solution registry. The `--local` flag tells the registry commands to walk up from CWD to find a `.uipx`, read the `resources/solution_folder/process/` files written by step 4, and surface every sibling project as a discoverable node type — all offline, without a tenant registry round-trip:
86	
87	```bash
88	# list every in-solution node type (all sibling projects)
89	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
90	
91	# fetch the full manifest for the coded agent
92	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json
93	```
94	
95	The second command's `Data.Node` object is what the flow skill pastes into the flow's `definitions[]`. For the node instance shape and top-level `bindings[]` entries, see the uipath-maestro-flow skill agent-plugin reference (In-solution variant).
96	
97	Without `--local`, `registry list`/`get` query the tenant registry (Orchestrator-published resources only) and will not surface the sibling project.
98	
99	## Wiring the Agent's Inputs
100	
101	For inputs that reference flow variables, use `{ "type": "literal", "expression": "{{ $vars.X }}", "fieldType": "string" }` — NOT `=js:...` expressions. `=js:` ships as a literal string to the agent activity and fails at runtime with `Cannot find name '<identifier>'`.
102	
103	Input-only rule. Mapping the agent's output back to a flow-level global on an End node DOES use `=js:` — see [variables-and-expressions.md § Variable Updates](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md#variable-updates-variableupdates).

1	# LangGraph Integration Guide
2	
3	How to build LangGraph agents that work with the UiPath platform. This guide covers project structure, entrypoint detection, LLM models, and common pitfalls.
4	
5	## Scaffolding a New Project
6	
7	If there is **no existing agent code**, scaffold a LangGraph project with:
8	
9	```bash
10	mkdir my-agent && cd my-agent
11	uip codedagent new my-agent
12	```
13	
14	This generates `main.py` (with a StateGraph template), `langgraph.json`, and `pyproject.toml`. Then modify `main.py` to implement your actual agent logic.
15	
16	> **Prerequisite:** `uipath-langchain` must be installed for the LangGraph template to be used. If you get a base template instead, install `uipath-langchain` first.
17	
18	## Project Structure
19	
20	LangGraph agents use a **different structure** from coded function agents. There are two supported patterns:
21	
22	### Pattern A: `langgraph.json` (Recommended for LangGraph)
23	
24	```
25	my-agent/
26	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
27	├── langgraph.json        # Graph configuration — maps names to graph variables
28	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies (must include uipath-langchain)
29	├── .env                  # Environment variables
30	└── ...                   # Generated by uip codedagent init
31	```
32	
33	**`langgraph.json`** tells the runtime where to find your graph:
34	
35	```json
36	{
37	  "graphs": {
38	    "agent": "./main.py:graph"
39	  }
40	}
41	```
42	
43	- `"agent"` — the entrypoint name (used with `uip codedagent run agent`)
44	- `"./main.py:graph"` — path to the Python file and the variable name (`file:variable`)
45	- The file can be named `main.py` or `graph.py` — just ensure the path matches
46	
47	### Pattern B: `uipath.json` with `functions`
48	
49	For agents that use `main.py` instead of `graph.py`:
50	
51	```
52	my-agent/
53	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
54	├── uipath.json           # UiPath config with functions mapping
55	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies
56	└── ...
57	```
58	
59	**`uipath.json`** maps the graph entrypoint:
60	
61	```json
62	{
63	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
64	  "runtimeOptions": {
65	    "isConversational": false
66	  },
67	  "packOptions": {
68	    "includeUvLock": true
69	  },
70	  "functions": {
71	    "graph": "main.py:graph"
72	  }
73	}
74	```
75	
76	### Which Pattern to Use?
77	
78	| Pattern | When to Use |
79	|---------|-------------|
80	| `langgraph.json` | New LangGraph projects, multi-graph setups |
81	| `uipath.json` functions | Existing UiPath projects adding a LangGraph graph |
82	
83	Both patterns require the `graph` variable to be a compiled `StateGraph` or `CompiledStateGraph`.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Required Dependencies
88	
89	Every LangGraph agent needs these in `pyproject.toml`:
90	
91	```toml
92	[project]
93	name = "my-agent"
94	version = "0.0.1"
95	description = "My LangGraph agent"
96	requires-python = ">=3.11"
97	dependencies = [
98	    "uipath",
99	    "uipath-langchain",
100	]
101	
102	[dependency-groups]
103	dev = [
104	    "uipath-dev",
105	]
106	```
107	
108	**Key point:** `uipath-langchain` is required — it registers the LangGraph runtime factory that enables `uip codedagent run`, `uip codedagent init`, and deployment to detect and execute your graph.
109	
110	For agents that use LLM calls, add the appropriate model dependency:
111	
112	```toml
113	dependencies = [
114	    "uipath",
115	    "uipath-langchain",
116	    "langgraph>=1.0.4",          # If using StateGraph directly
117	    "langchain-community",        # If using community tools (DuckDuckGo, etc.)
118	]
119	```
120	
121	---
122	
123	## LLM Models
124	
125	Use UiPath's LLM libraries instead of raw `langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI`. These route through UiPath's LLM Gateway for centralized model management and billing.
126	
127	### UiPathAzureChatOpenAI (Passthrough)
128	
129	Drop-in replacement for LangChain's `ChatOpenAI` that routes through UiPath's passthrough endpoint (Azure OpenAI API format). No API keys needed — usage consumes Agent Units from your UiPath account.
130	
131	Instantiate LLM clients inside graph nodes or functions — module-level instantiation fails during `uip codedagent init`. See [../lifecycle/build.md](../lifecycle/build.md) § Additional Instructions for the full rule.
132	
133	```python
134	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
135	
136	# Inside a graph node:
137	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(
138	    model="gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18",
139	    temperature=0.7,
140	    max_tokens=4000,
141	    timeout=30,
142	    max_retries=2
143	)
144	```
145	
146	**Model names:** Pass the model identifier as a string. Run `uip codedagent list-models` to list the models available in your tenant.
147	
148	**Features:**
149	- No API key needed — uses UiPath authentication
150	- Supports streaming, structured output, and tool calling
151	- Integrates seamlessly with LangChain agents and RAG
152	
153	### UiPathChat (Normalized)
154	
155	Versatile model class supporting multiple vendors through UiPath's normalized LLM Gateway API. Ideal for multi-vendor strategies.
156	
157	```python
158	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathChat
159	
160	llm = UiPathChat(
161	    model="gpt-4o-2024-11-20",
162	    temperature=0.5,
163	    max_tokens=2000
164	)
165	```
166	
167	**Supported Models Include:**
168	- **OpenAI**: `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `o3-mini-2025-01-31`
169	- **Anthropic**: `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0`
170	- **Google**: `gemini-2.0-flash-001`
171	- **AWS & Others**: Additional models based on your region and account
172	
173	**Features:**
174	- Supports multiple model providers
175	- Custom streaming headers for compatibility
176	- Flexible model switching for cost/quality optimization
177	- Regional availability may vary by data residency requirements
178	
179	### Configuration Parameters
180	
181	Both models support these configuration options:
182	
183	- `temperature` (0-1): Controls randomness vs. determinism (default: 0.7)
184	- `max_tokens`: Maximum response length (default varies by model)
185	- `timeout`: API request timeout in seconds
186	- `max_retries`: Number of retries on transient failures (default: 2)
187	- `top_p`: Nucleus sampling parameter for diversity
188	- `frequency_penalty`: Reduce token repetition
189	- `presence_penalty`: Encourage new topics
190	
191	### Structured Output
192	
193	Both models support `with_structured_output()` for Pydantic schema validation:
194	
195	```python
196	from pydantic import BaseModel
197	
198	class Analysis(BaseModel):
199	    sentiment: str
200	    confidence: float
201	
202	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
203	structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(Analysis)
204	raw_dict: dict = await structured_llm.ainvoke("Analyze: I love this product!")
205	result: Analysis = Analysis.model_validate(raw_dict)
206	```
207	
208	### Model Selection Guide
209	
210	| Use Case | Class |
211	|----------|-------|
212	| Cost-conscious, general tasks | `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
213	| Complex reasoning, state-of-the-art | `UiPathChat` or `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
214	| Multi-vendor flexibility (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) | `UiPathChat` |
215	| Specialized domains (e.g., code) | `UiPathChat` with a Claude model |
216	
217	Run `uip codedagent list-models` to see the model strings available in your tenant and pass the exact `model_name` to the class constructor.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Graph Definition
222	
223	### Input/Output Schemas
224	
225	Define `GraphInput` and `GraphOutput` as Pydantic models. These become the agent's schema for `uip codedagent init` and deployment:
226	
227	```python
228	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
229	
230	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
231	    query: str = Field(description="The user's question")
232	    max_results: int = Field(default=5, description="Max results to return")
233	
234	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
235	    answer: str = Field(description="The answer")
236	    sources: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Sources used")
237	```
238	
239	### State Definition
240	
241	Use `MessagesState` for agents that need conversation history, or a plain `TypedDict`/`BaseModel` for simpler workflows:
242	
243	```python
244	from langgraph.graph import MessagesState
245	
246	class GraphState(MessagesState):
247	    query: str
248	    answer: str | None = None
249	    sources: list[str] | None = None
250	```
251	
252	### Building the Graph
253	
254	```python
255	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph
256	from langgraph.types import Command
257	
258	async def search(state: GraphState) -> Command:
259	    # ... your logic ...
260	    return Command(update={"answer": "result", "sources": ["url1"]})
261	
262	builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
263	builder.add_node("search", search)
264	builder.add_edge(START, "search")
265	builder.add_edge("search", END)
266	
267	graph = builder.compile()
268	```
269	
270	**Important:** The variable MUST be named `graph` and be a `CompiledStateGraph`. This is what the runtime factory looks for.
271	
272	### Runtime Output Quirk — No Channel Reducers For Output Fields
273	
274	The UiPath LangGraph runtime captures the **last node's update delta** as the final output (`runtime.py` uses `stream_mode=["updates",...]` and overwrites `final_chunk` per event). Channel reducers like `Annotated[list, operator.add]` accumulate inside the graph but **do not appear in `--output-file` JSON or eval trajectories** — only the terminal node's delta does.
275	
276	For any aggregate field that must appear in the output, carry it forward explicitly instead of relying on a reducer:
277	
278	```python
279	return {"items": [*state.get("items", []), new_item]}
280	```
281	
282	Or have the terminal node compute the full aggregate and emit it.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## Tracing
287	
288	LangGraph agents get **automatic tracing** — you do NOT need `@traced()` on graph nodes. The UiPath LangGraph runtime instruments all node executions, LLM calls, and tool invocations automatically.
289	
290	Use `@traced()` only on helper functions **outside** the graph that you want to monitor:
291	
292	```python
293	from uipath.tracing import traced
294	
295	@traced(name="postprocess", span_type="tool")
296	async def postprocess(text: str) -> str:
297	    """This gets its own trace span because it's not a graph node."""
298	    return text.strip().lower()
299	```
300	
301	---
302	
303	## Running `uip codedagent init`
304	
305	After creating your graph, generate project configuration:
306	
307	```bash
308	uv sync
309	uip codedagent init
310	```
311	
312	### How Entrypoint Detection Works
313	
314	1. `uip codedagent init` loads all registered middleware via Python entry points
315	2. The `uipath-langchain` package registers a LangGraph middleware
316	3. The middleware checks for `langgraph.json` — if found, it handles init
317	4. If no `langgraph.json`, the standard init checks `uipath.json` `"functions"` field
318	5. The runtime imports your Python file and validates the `graph` variable
319	6. Input/Output schemas are extracted from the graph's `input`/`output` type annotations
320	
321	### Troubleshooting `uip codedagent init`
322	
323	**"No function entrypoints found"**
324	- Ensure `langgraph.json` exists with the correct `"graphs"` mapping, OR
325	- Ensure `uipath.json` has a `"functions"` entry pointing to your graph
326	- The file path and variable name must match exactly (e.g., `"./main.py:graph"`)
327	
328	**Import errors during init / authentication failures**
329	- `uip codedagent init` imports your Python file to introspect the graph
330	- Module-level `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()` or `UiPathChat()` will try to authenticate on import and fail
331	- **Fix: Move LLM instantiation inside functions/nodes, never at module level:**
332	  ```python
333	  # BAD — fails during uip codedagent init:
334	  llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
335	
336	  # GOOD — lazy initialization inside a node:
337	  async def my_node(state):
338	      llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
339	      return await llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
340	  ```
341	
342	**Schema not detected**
343	- Ensure your `StateGraph` specifies `input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput` 
344	- The Input/Output classes must be Pydantic `BaseModel` subclasses
345	
346	---
347	
348	## Running Your Agent
349	
350	```bash
351	# With langgraph.json
352	uip codedagent run agent '{"query": "What is Python?"}'
353	
354	# With uipath.json functions (using the function name)
355	uip codedagent run graph '{"query": "What is Python?"}'
356	```
357	
358	The entrypoint name comes from the key in `langgraph.json` `"graphs"` or `uipath.json` `"functions"`.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## Conversational Agents
363	
364	For the cross-framework contract (the `isConversational` flag, local-run options), see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md`.
365	
366	### In-Process Input
367	
368	Type the graph state's `messages` field as a list of `AnyMessage` with the `add_messages` reducer:
369	
370	```python
371	from typing import Annotated
372	from langchain_core.messages import AnyMessage
373	from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
374	from pydantic import BaseModel
375	
376	class State(BaseModel):
377	    messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add_messages] = []
378	```
379	
380	`langgraph.graph.MessagesState` is the equivalent shorthand.
381	
382	The wire envelope (see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md` § Wire Envelope) lands as the `messages` field; the `uipath-langchain` runtime converts each `UiPathConversationMessage` dict into a LangChain `HumanMessage` before the graph runs.
383	
384	### Two Implementation Options
385	
386	Both are valid — pick based on the agent's needs:
387	
388	- **Prebuilt ReAct agent** — `from langchain.agents import create_agent`. The input contract above is already wired in; just export the compiled graph from your entry point.
389	- **Custom graph** — any `StateGraph` topology consuming the same `messages` field. The first node can be fully deterministic (e.g. validation or routing) before any LLM call.
390	
391	### Local Run
392	
393	See `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md` § Running Locally for the `--keep-state-file` flag (required on every turn) and § Wire Envelope for the `turn1.json` shape.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## Available Tools
398	
399	The `uipath-langchain` package provides UiPath-specific LangChain tools:
400	
401	| Tool | Import | Purpose |
402	|------|--------|---------|
403	| Process invocation | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import create_process_tool` | Trigger UiPath processes |
404	| Escalation (HITL) | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import create_escalation_tool` | Send to human reviewer |
405	| Context search | `uipath_langchain.retrievers import ContextGroundingRetriever` | Search Context Grounding indexes |
406	| MCP tools | `uipath_langchain.agent.tools import open_mcp_tools` | Connect to MCP servers |
407	
408	> **Context Grounding retrieval in LangGraph:** always use `ContextGroundingRetriever` from `uipath_langchain.retrievers` — not `sdk.context_grounding.search()` / `search_async()`. The LangChain retriever integrates natively with the graph pipeline and auto-generates the correct `index` binding. See [../capabilities/context-grounding.md](../capabilities/context-grounding.md) for usage examples.
409

1	# Coded Agents — Flow Integration
2	
3	Coded agents in flows use the `uipath.core.agent.{key}` node with `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. Three patterns exist, distinguished by where the agent lives.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pattern 1: In-Solution Coded Agent
8	
9	The coded agent lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution as the flow. The flow references it with `section: "In this solution"`; the runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API.
10	
11	- **Agent-side scaffolding:** [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md)
12	- **Wiring the agent's inputs:** [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs)
13	- **Flow node JSON shape + top-level `bindings[]` + `definitions[]` entry:** uipath-maestro-flow skill, agent-plugin reference (In-solution variant)
14	
15	The node-type's `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution project add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) and surfaced by `uip maestro flow registry list --local`.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Pattern 2: Published Coded Agent
20	
21	The coded agent is deployed to Orchestrator as a standalone tenant resource. Any solution can reference it.
22	
23	**When to use:** reused across flows, independent versioning, already deployed.
24	
25	```bash
26	uip codedagent deploy --my-workspace
27	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
28	```
29	
30	**Capture the package key from the deploy command's own output** — `uip codedagent deploy` prints JSON containing the package `Key` (an Orchestrator-assigned GUID). That GUID is the `resourceKey` used in the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey`. Always run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` after deploy to refresh the local flow registry cache, but do NOT depend on `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` to return the deployed agent — that search only enumerates built-in node types (`uipath.agent.autonomous`, etc.); user-deployed coded agents do not appear there, so an empty result is the *expected* state and is NOT a sign the deploy failed.
31	
32	Fallback discovery paths if the deploy output is unavailable or unparseable, **tried in order** — stop at the first one that returns the package:
33	
34	1. `uip or packages list --search "<agent-name>" --output json` (tenant feed listing). Returns 404 on tenants where the caller lacks `Orchestrator.Packages.View` scope — if so, move to (2).
35	2. `uip or processes list --folder-path "<FolderName>" --output json` if the agent was deployed via `--folder` rather than `--my-workspace`.
36	
37	If all paths return empty / 404, the deploy command's stdout JSON is authoritative — re-run the deploy and capture its output rather than chasing post-hoc discovery endpoints.
38	
39	For the flow node JSON shape, see the uipath-maestro-flow skill agent-plugin reference (Published variant). `model.section` is `"Published"`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Pattern 3: Tool Resource for Another Agent
44	
45	The coded agent is a tool that another agent (inline or published) can call. Requires deploying the coded agent to Orchestrator first.
46	
47	**Resource file** at `<AgentProject>/resources/<ResourceName>/resource.json`:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "$resourceType": "tool",
52	  "type": "agent",
53	  "name": "MyCodedAgent",
54	  "description": "What this agent does (shown to the parent LLM for tool selection)",
55	  "location": "external",
56	  "properties": {
57	    "processName": "<CODED_AGENT_PROCESS_NAME>",
58	    "folderPath": "<FOLDER_PATH>"
59	  },
60	  "inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": { "userInput": { "type": "string" } } },
61	  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content":   { "type": "string" } } },
62	  "id": "<UUID>",
63	  "referenceKey": ""
64	}
65	```
66	
67	Coded agents use `location: "external"`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Pattern Comparison
72	
73	| Aspect | In-Solution (1) | Published (2) | Tool (3) |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Node type | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (local, from `project add`) | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (Orchestrator-assigned) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` |
76	| Lifecycle | `uip solution upload` (single pass) | `uip codedagent deploy` | `uip codedagent deploy` |
77	| Runtime lookup | Studio Web projects API | Orchestrator Releases API | Orchestrator (via parent agent) |
78	| `model.section` | `"In this solution"` | `"Published"` or absent | n/a |
79	| Cross-flow reuse | No | Yes | Yes |
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Debug
84	
85	| Error | Cause | Fix |
86	| --- | --- | --- |
87	| Node doesn't resolve in SW (Pattern 1) | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (it matches `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) |
88	| Agent not found in registry (Pattern 2/3) | Not deployed or registry stale | `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
89	| Tool resource never called | Tool description too vague | Sharpen the `description` in `resource.json` |
